args.text:
Okay, so. As part of the agency's Inspiration Tour flyover, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is gonna fly one of three F-5 fighter jets himself to kick off the New York Jets vs. Cleveland Browns gridiron game in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday, Oct. 11.

Before the game, NASA's crew'll be having a yarn with the fans at the agency's Experience Zone, set up at the Jets Tailgate Zone out the front of the stadium, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. EDT. Pop under the agency's Artemis dome and you can find out all about NASA heading back to the Moon, have a crack at the interactive games, and grab a happy snap with a whopping great blow-up SLS (Space Launch System) rocket.

The Inspiration Tour's doing stops right round the country, getting academic, industry and public sector players together and hooking the agency up with the people, technologies and organisations that keep the Yanks out in front in space.

It all winds up with MAX POWER, a public expo of American air and space know-how, on Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8, on and round the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. It's being held to mark America's historic 250th anniversary, and the multi-day, family-friendly do'll show off the next lot of aircraft, spacecraft, driverless vehicles and technologies that'll help shape how we get about in air and space down the track.
